requirements.evidence: Contract and most requirements are implemented and coherent: EntityInvite model with role/datetime casts and lowercasing saving hook (app/Models/EntityInvite.php:10-38), migration with cascade/nullable FKs, default role and unique (entity_id,email) (database/migrations/2026_10_29_062141_create_entity_invites_table.php:14-25), Entity::invites() (app/Models/Entity.php:41-44), sendInvite validation/duplicate/race/rate-limit/reset (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:44-118), cancelInvite (Members.php:121-133), accept/decline with 403, expiry error on 'invite', idempotent accepted, firstOrCreate membership, session + redirect (app/Livewire/Entity/PendingInvites.php:14-71), manager-only mount and route (Members.php:38-42, routes/web.php:56), openMember prefill + not-found behaviour (Members.php:135-148), saveRole/confirmRemoval/cancelRemoval/removeMember rules (Members.php:150-218), exact modal title and no-empty-option select (resources/views/livewire/entity/members.blade.php:82-95), mailable + markdown view + pt_BR strings (app/Mail/EntityInviteMail.php:13-37, resources/views/emails/entity-invite.blade.php:1-16, lang/pt_BR.json:865-882). Gaps: accepted invites are also deleted on re-invite (Members.php:84-90), the owner draft role cannot be represented by the admin/employee select (members.blade.php:92-95), and the 'existing PegaFila theme' claim cannot be verified because the view relies on mail::message (entity-invite.blade.php:1).

conventions.evidence: Follows most conventions: generated-style migration with reversible down() (migration:12-34), #[Validate] on the invite properties (Members.php:26-30), enum cast and typed factory with expired() state (EntityInvite.php:18-24, database/factories/EntityInviteFactory.php:21-38), Blade component x-input and Bulma markup (members.blade.php:14-22), CHANGELOG and docs/database-schema.md updated. Deviations: no tests at all, new domain writes stay in Livewire components instead of app/Actions/* (Members.php:83-108, PendingInvites.php:32-44), three added ui keys are never used while the same strings are also added as JSON keys (lang/en/ui.php:78-80 vs lang/pt_BR.json:865-867), `#[Fillable]` attribute instead of the `$fillable` property (EntityInvite.php:10), and docs/business-rules.md is not updated for the new invite invariant.

security.evidence: Good baseline: every write action authorizes server-side (Members.php:40,46,123,137,152,156,184,198) and re-resolves client-supplied ids inside $this->entity (Members.php:125,141,154,196); accept/decline enforce the e-mail owner with 403 (PendingInvites.php:20,63); invite success is rate-limited per manager+entity (Members.php:77,106); all output uses {{ }} auto-escaping. Gaps with limited impact: selectedMembershipId is a public client-writable record id without #[Locked] (Members.php:32), cancelRemoval() has no authorize() call (Members.php:189-192), memberRole is validated inline rather than via #[Validate] (Members.php:34,158), and the can:update,entity guard is only route middleware, not registered with Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware (routes/web.php:56), so it does not re-apply to Livewire updates (per-action authorize limits the impact).

tests.evidence: change.diff contains no tests/** additions or modifications; the file list ends at routes/web.php:56. Conventions require a Pest/PHPUnit test for every feature plus unauthorized-call and tamper tests for each Livewire action, including the duplicate/unique-race path, the 10/hour rate limit, accept/decline ownership, owner immutability and last-manager rules; none are covered.

simplicity.evidence: Lean and direct overall: reuses x-input, existing ui keys, the audit log channel and Eloquent relations; no new service/repository layer and no JS. Some duplication: the pending-invite predicate is repeated (Members.php:63-67 and 224-228, PendingInvites.php:80-87) and the `role instanceof UserRole` fallback appears three times (Members.php:143-146, PendingInvites.php:38-40, entity-invite.blade.php:4) even though the cast always yields UserRole; isPending()/isExpired() (EntityInvite.php:46-54) are unused.

readability.evidence: Clear names and focused methods (Members.php:44-118, 121-218; PendingInvites.php:14-92), consistent with sibling style; Blade is readable. Minor issues: sendInvite is ~75 lines, the added outer <div> at members.blade.php:5 does not re-indent the existing card block, the modal close button hardcodes aria-label="close" (members.blade.php:83), and the three unused ui keys are dead additions.

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task (models, migration, factory, mail, components, views, lang, routes, docs). Out-of-scope noise: unrelated JSON slash-escaping churn on pre-existing keys (lang/pt_BR.json:532,644,789,863) and deleting accepted invite rows before re-inviting, which the task did not ask for (Members.php:84-90).

issues.explanation: The change ships zero Pest/PHPUnit tests, although the project mandates a test for every feature and unauthorized-call plus tamper tests for every Livewire action; the whole invite flow (send, duplicate/race, rate limit, accept/decline, save role, removal) is unverified.

selectedMembershipId (a record id) and confirmingRemoval (a flag) are public and client-writable without #[Locked], and memberRole has no #[Validate], violating the project's Livewire security policy rule 2; impact is limited only because each action re-resolves the id inside $this->entity and authorizes.

The manager guard is added as route middleware `can:update,entity`, but it is not registered with Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware, so it silently stops applying on subsequent Livewire update requests (security rule 6); per-action authorize() calls mitigate the impact.
cancelRemoval() performs no authorization, unlike every other public action, which breaks the 'authorize every action' rule even though it only resets a boolean.

accept() and decline() read auth()->user()->email without an auth()->check() guard (render() has one), so a guest invocation against the Livewire endpoint would error instead of returning a clean denial.
sendInvite deletes any accepted invite rows for the e-mail before inserting, while the task only permits replacing an expired pending invite, so accepted invite history is silently destroyed.

For an owner membership openMember() prefills memberRole with 'owner' (Members.php:143-146), but the select only offers admin/employee, so the control displays a value that does not match the draft; the required no-empty-option rule prevents representing the current role.

New domain writes (creating an invite, creating a membership on accept, role/removal changes) are done directly in Livewire components instead of dedicated app/Actions/* classes with authorization inside, which the conventions require for domain writes.

ui.members_title, ui.members_invite_title and ui.members_invite_submit are added in both locales but never used; the Blade uses the duplicate JSON translations (lang/pt_BR.json:865-867) for the same strings instead.
The new invite-only membership invariant is a business rule, but only docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md were updated; the conventions require docs/business-rules.md to stay in sync.

Mass assignment is declared with the newer #[Fillable] PHP attribute instead of a $fillable property; verify the pinned Laravel version supports it and that sibling models use this style, otherwise the model will fail to load or diverge from the codebase style.
isPending() and isExpired() are unused dead helpers, and the role instanceof UserRole fallback is repeated in three places although the enum cast always returns UserRole.

Pre-existing keys were rewritten only to escape forward slashes ("Press \/ to search", "State \/ County", "Uploading files...", "Zip \/ Postal Code"), an unrelated JSON reserialization with no behaviour change.
confirmRemoval() opens the confirmation modal while the details modal stays is-active, so two Bulma modals are stacked at once; hiding the details modal during confirmation would be clearer.
The new outer <div> wrapper is added without re-indenting the existing card block, and the modal close button's aria-label="close" is hardcoded English instead of a translation key.

review.summary: The change implements the invite-only membership feature broadly to spec: entity_invites migration/model/factory, queued markdown invite mail with pt_BR strings, a manager-only members page with invite/pending lists and detail/removal modals, and a PendingInvites component wired into the switcher and onboarding. It ships no tests at all and has several Livewire-policy gaps (unlocked selectedMembershipId, non-persistent route middleware, unauthorized cancelRemoval), plus small requirement and duplication issues, so it needs substantial rework before merging.
